13 Corporate Drive, Halfmoon, NY 12065 
lspowergrid.com  
November 16, 2026 
VIA ETARIFF 
The Honorable Debbie-Anne A. Reese 
Secretary 
Federal Energy Regulatory Commission 
888 First Street, N.E. 
 
Washington, D.C. 20426 
 
Re:  
LS Power Grid New York Corporation I, Docket No. ER27-___-000 
New York Independent System Operator, Inc., Docket No. EL26-69-000 
Proposed Revisions to Rate Schedule 10 of the NYISO OATT to Provide 
for Large Load-Driven Upgrade Cost Recovery 
 
Dear Secretary Reese: 
Pursuant to section 205 of the Federal Power Act (“FPA”)1 and Part 35 of the 
Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s (“FERC” or “Commission”) regulations, 2 and 
in response to the Commission’s order instituting the show-cause proceeding in 
New York Independent System Operator, Inc.,3 LS Power Grid New York Corporation 
I (“LS Power Grid”)4 submits revisions to Section 6.10 (Rate Schedule 10) of the 
NYISO OATT, specifically the generally applicable provisions of Rate Schedule 10 
and LS Power Grid’s company-specific provisions in Attachment 1 to Rate Schedule 
10, Section 6.10.7. LS Power Grid respectfully requests that the Commission accept 
the proposed tariff revisions to become effective January 16, 2027, sixty-one (61) 
days after filing, consistent with the Commission’s prior notice requirement, 5 and 
grant any necessary waivers. 
 
1 16 U.S.C. § 824d (2022). 
2 18 C.F.R. Pt. 35 (2026). 
3 195 FERC ¶ 61,216 (2026) (“Show Cause Order”). 
4 The New York Independent System Operator, Inc. ("NYISO") is submitting this ﬁling via eTariff on 
behalf of LS Power Grid solely in its role as the tariff administrator of the NYISO Open Access 
Transmission Tariff ("OATT"). The burden of demonstrating that the proposed tariff amendments are 
just and reasonable rests with LS Power Grid, the sponsoring party. The NYISO takes no position on 
any substantive aspect of the ﬁling at this time and reserves the right to ﬁle comments and/or 
protest the ﬁling. 
5 18 C.F.R. § 35.3(a)(1).

Page 2 
I. 
Introduction and Summary of Filing 
The proposed revisions establish a transparent, company-specific mechanism for 
LS Power Grid to recover the costs of transmission upgrades that are identified as 
necessary, in whole or in part, to provide transmission service to an Eligible 
Customer6 on behalf of a Large Load (“Large Load-Driven Upgrades”). The revisions 
include a pro forma Large Load Cost Recovery Agreement (“CRA”), revisions to the 
Formula Rate Template (“Template”) and Formula Rate Implementation Protocols 
(“Protocols”), cost-allocation provisions, and new Rate Schedule 10 provisions 
governing NYISO billing, collection, security, remittance, data exchange, and formula 
rate treatment of CRA amounts. 
The filing responds to the Commission’s preliminary concerns regarding potential 
cost shifting by assigning the wholesale payment obligation to the Eligible 
Customer that takes or requests transmission service on behalf of the Large Load 
Facility and by requiring Construction Security, Operational Security, NYISO billing 
and collection, Security-draw procedures, and direct collection rights. The 
framework is designed to mitigate the risk that other customers bear costs 
associated with a Large Load Facility that is delayed, reduced, or does not 
materialize, while preserving NYISO’s existing roles and LS Power Grid’s Formula 
Rate recovery. 
No Large Load-Driven Upgrade is listed in proposed Table 1 as of the requested 
effective date. Accordingly, the filing does not change currently effective Regulated 
Transmission Facilities Charge (“RTFC”) rates under the NYISO OATT or impose a 
Large Load Charge on any customer upon effectiveness. The proposed revisions 
also make conforming corrections to existing Formula Rate Template and Protocol 
provisions, including provisions governing the cost-of-capital and true-up 
calculations. Those corrections do not revise the currently effective RTFC; they will 
be reflected, as applicable, in future Annual Projections, Annual Updates, and True-
Up Adjustments under the Formula Rate. An individual Large Load-Driven Upgrade 
may be included in the RTFC only after a separate FPA section 205 filing adds that 
upgrade to Table 1 and the Commission accepts the designation. 
 
6 Capitalized terms used but not otherwise deﬁned in this transmittal letter have the meanings 
assigned to them in the NYISO OATT, including the proposed revisions to Rate Schedule 10 and 
Attachment 1 thereto, the proposed pro forma Large Load Cost Recovery Agreement (“CRA”) set forth 
in Appendix 1 to Attachment 1, and, as applicable, the proposed Formula Rate Template and Formula 
Rate Implementation Protocols.

Page 3 
II. 
Background 
A. LS Power Grid and its Rate Schedule 10 Recovery 
LS Power Grid is a non-incumbent Transmission Owner in the NYISO region. LS 
Power Grid and the New York Power Authority (“NYPA”) developed Segment A of 
the AC Transmission Public Policy Transmission Need, a 345 kV project between the 
Marcy/Edic and New Scotland substations (“AC Transmission Project”), which is 
now in service as part of Central East Energy Connect. LS Power Grid has no 
franchised retail service territory and no Transmission Service Charge under 
Attachment H of the NYISO OATT. LS Power Grid currently recovers its 
Commission-accepted revenue requirement exclusively under Rate Schedule 10 
through its formula rate and the associated RTFC. 
B. Show Cause Order and Stakeholder Process 
On June 18, 2026, the Commission issued the Show Cause Order, instituting a 
section 206 proceeding in Docket No. EL26-69-000 and identifying concerns 
about cost shifting, transparency, minimum-revenue commitments, credit support, 
and the rate treatment of large load payments.7 The Commission later granted 
abeyance through November 16, 2026, for respondents that make timely section 
205 filings addressing its preliminary findings.8 
LS Power Grid participated in NYISO and stakeholder discussions concerning large 
load integration and cost recovery. Those discussions confirmed that a 
transmission owner without retail customers needs a wholesale mechanism to 
protect its other transmission customers when a Large Load Facility requires a 
Large Load-Driven Upgrade to that transmission owner’s facilities. LS Power Grid’s 
proposal is designed to operate alongside NYISO’s study and interconnection 
procedures. It does not displace the separate arrangements that an Eligible 
Customer must enter into with the owner of an Affected System for an Affected 
System Upgrade.9 
III. 
Description of the Proposed Revisions 
A. Rate Schedule 10 Eligibility and Cost Allocation 
New Section 6.10.1.1(xii) identifies a Large Load-Driven Upgrade of a Transmission 
Owner or Other Developer that does not recover a transmission revenue 
 
7 Show Cause Order at PP 72-91. 
8 N.Y. Indep. Sys. Operator, Inc., 196 FERC ¶ 61,130 (2026) (granting abeyance). 
9 See CRA §§ 4.2 and 6.2 and Schedule 1.

Page 4 
requirement through an Attachment H Transmission Service Charge or NYPA 
Transmission Adjustment Charge as an eligible project category, subject to 
Commission acceptance of the applicable Transmission Owner’s or Other 
Developer’s designation. Section 6.10.1.2 confirms that the otherwise-applicable 
exclusion for projects outside Attachment Y does not exclude such an eligible Large 
Load-Driven Upgrade. The definition cross-references NYISO’s proposed definition 
of “Large Load” in Section 1.12 of the OATT, which is separately being filed. The 
provisions preserve the exclusion for directly assigned facilities that are paid by the 
Eligible Customer and not included in the Transmission Owner’s rate base. 
Under Sections 6.10.3.7.2 and 6.10.7.3.2, a Large Load-Driven Upgrade becomes an 
Eligible Project only after Commission acceptance of a section 205 filing adding it 
to Table 1. That section 205 designation filing will provide the appropriate 
opportunity to evaluate the particular upgrade, the supporting study record, and 
the application of the CRA protections before the upgrade is included in the RTFC. 
Each designated Large Load-Driven Upgrade is recovered together with the AC 
Transmission Project through a single RTFC and allocated to Responsible LSEs in 
the same manner as the AC Transmission Project. The assignment, reassignment, 
reduction, or cessation of service by the Large Load does not itself modify that 
Commission-accepted RTFC allocation. 
B. Pro Forma CRA 
The pro forma CRA and Limited Acknowledgment are included as Appendix 1 to 
Attachment 1 to Rate Schedule 10, Section 6.10.7.5.1. The CRA is entered into by LS 
Power Grid and the Eligible Customer. The Large Load Customer executes a Limited 
Acknowledgment but does not become a party to the Eligible Customer’s wholesale 
payment obligations. NYISO is not a party to the CRA; its billing, collection, security, 
remittance, and data functions arise under the Rate Schedule 10 Large Load 
Provisions.10  
For each Covered Upgrade, the CRA establishes a fixed Annual Minimum 
Transmission Revenue Contribution (“Annual MTRC”) under the Schedule 5 MTRC 
Calculation Template. The Annual MTRC is initially estimated and is redetermined to 
the Final Annual MTRC on the Final MTRC Determination Date, which occurs no later 
than one year after the applicable Upgrade In-Service Date after actual capital 
costs are known and accounted for. Schedule 5 uses the applicable capital 
structure, return on equity, cost of debt, tax, depreciation, and expense-allocation 
inputs to establish the levelized Fixed Charge Rate and Final Annual MTRC. The 
 
10 See id. Article 1 and Limited Acknowledgment; Rate Schedule 10 §§ 6.10.3.7 and 6.10.7.4.

Page 5 
MTRC Term begins on the actual Upgrade In-Service Date and ends on the day 
immediately preceding its twentieth anniversary, with the first and final Rate Years 
prorated. The CRA does not reset the final contractual Annual MTRC through 
ordinary annual formula rate updates, except for the limited prospective 
adjustments expressly identified in the CRA.11 
The twenty-year MTRC Term is a defined contractual revenue-support period, not 
the depreciable life of a Covered Upgrade. Schedule 5 establishes a levelized 
Annual MTRC for that period, while the Covered Upgrade remains subject to 
ordinary Formula Rate depreciation and other cost-of-service treatment. The term 
provides a substantial, predictable period of revenue responsibility for the Large 
Load-Driven Upgrade and is reinforced by Operational Security based on the 
remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility and a Termination Fee equal to that 
remaining responsibility less any Supplemental MTRC already billed and remaining 
unpaid upon an early termination or permanent cessation of service. The excluded 
unpaid bills remain separately payable.12 
The Eligible Customer owes a Supplemental MTRC to the extent Qualifying 
Transmission Revenues attributable to the Large Load Facility are less than the 
applicable Annual MTRC. The CRA provides for annual reconciliation. Construction 
Security protects pre-service commitments and cancellation exposure. After an 
upgrade enters service, Operational Security equals the nominal remaining 
Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, subject to Qualifying Retail Security Support 
that is legally available for the corresponding wholesale obligation. A termination or 
permanent cessation after in-service triggers a Termination Fee equal to the 
Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility less any Supplemental MTRC already 
billed and remaining unpaid as of the effective termination or cessation date, as 
provided in CRA Section 3.3.4. Those unpaid bills remain separately payable as 
Large Load Charges. NYISO’s receipt of the Termination Fee in full discharges only 
the remaining responsibility included in the fee and does not discharge the 
excluded unpaid bills. The Termination Fee is an accelerated contractual 
termination charge, not a penalty. Rather than producing a one-time Formula Rate 
Credit, the Termination Fee Balance is held by NYISO and remitted as Annual 
Termination Fee Remittances over the remaining MTRC Term, so the resulting 
Formula Rate Credits follow the annual schedule that would have applied absent 
termination.13 
 
11 See CRA §§ 3.2 and 6.3.1 and Schedule 5. 
12 See id. §§ 3.3.4–3.3.6, 6.3, 6.7, and Article 7; Schedule 5. 
13 See id. §§ 3.3.4–3.3.6, 6.4–6.8, and Article 7; Rate Schedule 10 § 6.10.7.4.

Page 6 
The CRA requires Operational Security equal to one hundred percent (100%) of the 
nominal Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility. The Commission 
preliminarily found that “an Eligible Customer may include a credit support or other 
financial security posted by a large load as part of a retail agreement to avoid 
creating duplicative credit support requirements.”14 To avoid duplicative collateral, 
the direct Operational Security requirement may be reduced dollar-for-dollar by 
qualifying retail security support only where the Eligible Customer delivers a current 
Retail Security Certification. The certification must confirm that the retail Large 
Load Customer has posted security available to the Eligible Customer for the 
corresponding wholesale obligations and that the Eligible Customer has 
enforceable draw or application rights, or the benefit of a binding undertaking, 
permitting it to use the proceeds for that purpose. Qualifying retail security support 
does not reduce the Eligible Customer’s underlying payment obligations, does not 
apply to Construction Security or Pre-In-Service Termination Costs, and is subject 
to notice and verification requirements if the support is reduced, drawn, expires, is 
not renewed, or otherwise may be impaired.15 
LS Power Grid recognizes that, after further stakeholder experience and discussion, 
a lower Operational Security requirement may be appropriate in defined 
circumstances where an alternative credit support arrangement provides 
equivalent protection against a cost shift. The Show Cause Order also invited 
further consideration of alternative mechanisms that could provide comparable or 
greater protection against cost shifting.16 This filing nonetheless adopts a 
conservative requirement of Operational Security equal to one hundred percent 
(100%) of the nominal Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility, subject only 
to the limited treatment of qualifying retail security support described above. LS 
Power Grid intends to work with NYISO and interested stakeholders to evaluate 
whether, and under what objectively defined circumstances, a different security 
level or alternative credit support structure could provide comparable protection. 
Any future change to the security requirement would be submitted to the 
Commission for review and acceptance under section 205 of the Federal Power 
Act. 
C. Revenue Attribution, Allocation, and Rate Treatment 
Qualifying Transmission Revenues are not a separate retail or load-based charge 
imposed by LS Power Grid. They are the portion of RTFC revenues assessed on the 
 
14 Show Cause Order at P 89. 
15 See CRA Article 7 and Schedule 3. 
16 Show Cause Order at PP 88–89.

Page 7 
Actual Energy Withdrawals of the Large Load Facility, collected from the 
Responsible LSE or LSEs serving that facility, and remitted to LS Power Grid that is 
attributable to the applicable Covered Upgrade and reduces the RTFC otherwise 
collected from other Responsible LSEs. Schedule 2 to the CRA provides a 
reproducible methodology using the applicable metering data, RTFC rate, Load 
Zone or Subzone allocation, and Covered Upgrade Revenue Share.17 
Where an upgrade is driven by more than one Large Load Facility, Schedule 1 
identifies an Initial Allocation Percentage for each Large Load Customer based on 
the applicable final study and allocation methodology. That allocation accounts for 
the large loads studied individually, jointly, or in a cluster; their differing requested 
service levels, development phases, and facility configurations; and any portion of 
the facility that serves other system needs or customers. The aggregate allocation 
to all Large Load Customers may not exceed one hundred percent (100%), and any 
unallocated portion remains subject to the otherwise applicable Rate Schedule 10 
cost-allocation and recovery rules.18 
The CRA does not itself determine whether a facility is directly assigned or included 
in rate base. That determination is made under the applicable NYISO tariff, study 
process, and interconnection arrangements. Direct Assignment Facilities and other 
facilities whose costs are directly assigned to, and paid by, the Eligible Customer 
and are not included in LS Power Grid’s rate base are excluded from the definition 
of Large Load-Driven Upgrades and from the MTRC framework.19 
Covered Upgrades are separately identified in LS Power Grid’s Formula Rate and 
use the capital structure and generally applicable return components applicable to 
LS Power Grid under Rate Schedule 10, including any Commission-approved 
generally applicable return on equity incentive, as applicable. Covered Upgrades do 
not receive return on equity incentives that are specific to the AC Transmission 
Project or become subject to the AC Transmission Project’s Competitive Bid 
Concession, cost cap, or other project-specific cost-containment commitments.20 
 
17 See CRA § 6.2 and Schedule 2. 
18 See id. § 6.3.2–6.3.4 and Schedule 1. 
19 See id. §§ 2.37 (deﬁnition of “Large Load-Driven Upgrades”), 6.2. 
20 See id. § 6.2 and Arzola Testimony.

Page 8 
D. NYISO Billing Security and Remittance Functions 
New Section 6.10.3.7 confirms that the Attachment-level Large Load Provisions are 
part of Rate Schedule 10, directs NYISO to perform the functions assigned to it 
under those provisions, distinguishes Large Load Charges from RTFC charges and 
revenues, and confirms that NYISO does not become a party to a Large Load CRA. 
New Section 6.10.7.4 requires execution of an applicable CRA and delivery of 
Construction Security before LS Power Grid undertakes specified construction 
commitments. It directs NYISO to bill customer-specific Large Load Charges based 
on LS Power Grid Charge Statements; hold and administer CRA Security; draw and 
apply Security under defined conditions; hold and remit Termination Fees; provide 
load and settlement data; and remit collected amounts to LS Power Grid. The 
provision separately identifies these charges from RTFC charges and preserves 
applicable NYISO billing and dispute procedures.21  
The proposed Template and Protocols provide the rate treatment and supporting 
workpapers. In the Annual Projection, Large Load CRA Revenue consists of 
projected Supplemental MTRC, including any prior-period Supplemental MTRC 
true-up adjustment, and projected Annual Termination Fee Remittances. In the 
Annual Update, the Formula Rate Credit reflects Actual Large Load CRA Revenue 
actually received by LS Power Grid during the Rate Year, including Supplemental 
MTRC payments collected and remitted by NYISO, Applied Security Proceeds 
applied and remitted to LS Power Grid, direct recoveries from an Eligible Customer 
applied to Supplemental MTRC obligations, and Annual Termination Fee 
Remittances. The Annual Update replaces the projected credit with actual cash 
receipts, and any difference is addressed through the Formula Rate true-up 
mechanism in the next Rate Year, with the applicable Formula Rate interest 
treatment. An Eligible Customer remains liable for all unpaid Large Load Charges, 
and the CRA’s Security and collection provisions are designed to mitigate the risk of 
nonpayment.22 
E. Supporting Testimony and Illustrative Exhibits 
Mr. Patrick Hayes’ testimony (Exhibit No. GNY-100) explains the need for the CRA 
framework and describes the operation of the Annual MTRC, Supplemental MTRC, 
revenue responsibility, security, and termination provisions. His supporting exhibits 
provide an illustrative MTRC Calculation (Exhibit No. GNY-101), an example 
Reconciliation Statement (Exhibit No. GNY-102), and an example Charge Statement 
 
21 See Rate Schedule 10 §§ 6.10.3.7 and 6.10.7.4; CRA Articles 5 and 7. 
22 See CRA §§ 6.10.7.4.5, 6.10.7.4.7, and 6.10.7.4.11; CRA §§ 6.6, 6.8, 6.13.5, and Article 7.

Page 9 
(Exhibit No. GNY-103), each of which tracks the corresponding provisions of the 
CRA, including Schedule 5 and Sections 6.4 through 6.8. 
Mr. D. Eric Arzola’s testimony (Exhibit No. GNY-200) sponsors the Template and 
Protocol revisions and explains the Formula Rate Credit for Large Load CRA 
Revenue. His supporting exhibits include the clean and marked Formula Rate 
Templates (Exhibit Nos. GNY-201 and GNY-202), the clean Formula Rate Template 
in native Excel format with all formula intact (Exhibit No. GNY-203), an illustrative 
Formula Rate Template – Annual Projection (Exhibit No. GNY-204), an illustrative 
Formula Rate Template – Annual Update (Exhibit No. GNY-205), and the clean and 
marked Formula Rate Implementation Protocols (Exhibit Nos. GNY-206 and GNY-
207). Exhibit No. GNY-205 illustrates the Annual Update, including the customer-
level Supplemental MTRC true-up and the ordinary Formula Rate true-up of 
projected CRA revenue credits to actual receipts. Together, those materials 
demonstrate the projected, annual-update, and true-up treatment of Supplemental 
MTRC and Annual Termination Fee Remittances. 
IV. 
The Proposed Revisions Are Just and Reasonable 
The proposal materially mitigates the cost-shifting concern identified in the Show 
Cause Order. Before in-service, Construction Security and termination-cost 
provisions protect against cancellation and related exposure. After an upgrade 
enters service, the Annual MTRC, Supplemental MTRC, Required Operational 
Security, and termination provisions establish a defined revenue responsibility 
associated with the service request that caused the upgrade. Required Operational 
Security equals one hundred percent (100%) of the nominal Remaining Cumulative 
Revenue Responsibility, subject to any qualifying retail-security support recognized 
under the CRA. NYISO billing, mandatory Security draws, and LS Power Grid’s direct 
collection rights further protect against nonpayment. 
The proposal also supplies the transparency and crediting mechanisms the 
Commission identified. The pro forma CRA in Appendix 1, Table 1, Schedules 1 and 5, 
the Template and Protocol workpapers, and the Annual Projection and Annual 
Update provide a traceable record of the relevant upgrades, customer obligations, 
credits, billings, and reconciliations. The illustrative MTRC Calculation (Exhibit No. 
GNY-101), example Reconciliation Statement (Exhibit No. GNY-102), and example 
Charge Statement (Exhibit No. GNY-103) further demonstrate the calculation and 
administration of these requirements. Customer-specific information is protected 
under CRA § 6.12 and Protocols § 8, while the required public information remains 
available in aggregated or redacted form as appropriate.

Page 10 
The proposed use of the existing Rate Schedule 10 RTFC allocation does not assign 
responsibility for a Large Load-Driven Upgrade to Responsible LSEs on the theory 
that those LSEs caused the underlying Large Load Facility or its service request. 
Rather, once the Commission accepts a designation of a Covered Upgrade in Table 
1, the existing RTFC provides the established mechanism for collecting LS Power 
Grid’s Commission-authorized revenue requirement for that transmission facility. 
The CRA separately requires the Eligible Customer serving the Large Load Facility to 
provide the Annual MTRC through Qualifying Transmission Revenues and 
Supplemental MTRC payments, and the Formula Rate credits Actual Large Load 
CRA Revenue dollar-for-dollar against LS Power Grid’s revenue requirement. Thus, 
the RTFC allocation supplies the collection path, while the CRA framework assigns 
the relevant payment obligation to the Eligible Customer and materially mitigates 
the associated risk through Security, NYISO billing and collection, and direct 
enforcement rights. 
Finally, the proposal is appropriately tailored to LS Power Grid. It provides a cost-
recovery and security path for a non-incumbent Transmission Owner with no retail 
customers or Attachment H Transmission Service Charge. It does not disturb the 
current AC Transmission Project allocation, existing RTFC recovery, NYISO study 
authority, or the retail arrangements between an Eligible Customer and a Large 
Load Customer. 
V. 
Requested Effective Date and Waivers 
LS Power Grid requests an effective date of January 16, 2027, sixty-one (61) days 
after the date of this filing, satisfying the Commission’s sixty-day notice 
requirement.23 LS Power Grid requests waiver of the cost-of-service-statement 
requirements of 18 C.F.R. § 35.13, and any other Part 35 requirements that otherwise 
may apply, to the extent necessary. The requested waivers are appropriate 
because the filing establishes a prospective formula rate and contractual 
framework, identifies no Large Load-Driven Upgrade in Table 1, does not change 
currently effective RTFC rates, and makes only conforming Formula Rate Template 
and Protocol corrections that will be implemented through the ordinary formula-
rate processes. 
VI. 
Contents of Filing 
LS Power Grid submits the following materials: 
• This transmittal letter; 
 
23 18 C.F.R. § 35.3(a)(1).

Page 11 
• Clean and marked tariff records revising Rate Schedule 10 and Attachment 1 
to Rate Schedule 10, including the proposed changes in Sections 6.10.7.3 
through 6.10.7.5 and the pro forma CRA and Limited Acknowledgment in 
Appendix 1, Section 6.10.7.5.1; 
• Direct testimony of Patrick Hayes (Exhibit No. GNY-100) and supporting 
exhibits: illustrative MTRC Calculation (Exhibit No. GNY-101), example 
Reconciliation Statement (Exhibit No. GNY-102), and example Charge 
Statement (Exhibit No. GNY-103); and 
• Direct testimony of D. Eric Arzola (Exhibit No. GNY-200) and supporting 
exhibits: clean and marked Formula Rate Templates (Exhibit Nos. GNY-201 
and GNY-202), clean Formula Rate Template in native Excel format with all 
formulas intact (Exhibit No. GNY-203), illustrative Formula Rate Template – 
Annual Projection (Exhibit No. GNY-204), illustrative Formula Rate Template – 
Annual Update (Exhibit No. GNY-205), and clean and marked Formula Rate 
Implementation Protocols (Exhibit Nos. GNY-206 and GNY-207), 
demonstrating the customer-level Supplemental MTRC true-up and the 
ordinary Formula Rate true-up of projected CRA revenue credits to actual 
receipts. 
VII. 
Communications and Service 
LS Power Grid requests that all pleadings, correspondence, and other 
communications concerning this matter be directed to the following persons, and 
their names and addresses be placed on the official service list for this docket:

LS Power Grid has confirmed with the NYISO that a complete copy of this filing will 
be posted on the NYISO’s website at www.nyiso.com. The NYISO has also informed 
LS Power Grid that it will send an electronic link to this filing to the official 
representative of each its customers and each participant on its stakeholder 
committees. Additionally, LS Power Grid has served a copy of this filing on the

under the Commission’s regulations.

Page 12 
VIII. 
Conclusion 
For the reasons stated above and in the supporting testimony, LS Power Grid 
respectfully requests that the Commission accept the proposed tariff revisions 
effective January 16, 2027, subject to the requested waivers. 
 
Respectfully submitted,
